Aged Care Legislation Amendment (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Aged Care Commissioner and Other Measures) Bill 2026

EAGAR, Professor Kathleen (Kathy), Private capacity [by video link]

YATES, Mr Ian, Private capacity [by video link]

Committee met at 13 : 01

CHAIR ( Senator Whiteaker ): I declare open this afternoon's hearing of the Community Affairs Legislation Committee's inquiry into the Aged Care Legislation Amendment (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Aged Care Commissioner and Other Measures) Bill 2026. We are joined this morning by Kathy Eagar and Ian Yates. Thank you for making time, particularly at such short notice, to give evidence to the inquiry today. I understand that information on parliamentary privilege and the protection and obligations of witnesses has been provided to you. I remind senators of their obligations under the Behaviour Code for parliamentarians.

Mr Yates : I am a former acting Inspector-General of Aged Care and was chief executive of COTA Australia for two decades and have had many other roles that I won't go through.

Senator RUSTON: Thank you very much, Mr Yates and Professor Eagar. I have to confess, Professor Eagar, I'm one of the people having a little trouble hearing what you're saying, but I've certainly picked up enough of it to get the vibe. This is to you, particularly, Professor Eagar. You've previously described to the committee how a one-point difference in the functional independence score can mean a $40,000 difference in funding, and that cognition, mental health, frailty and carer needs are considered too late to have much effect. As to the examples you used, do you think Greta and Yasmine would even qualify for this pathway, given the supplementary explanatory memorandum says that a request must point to circumstances that were not used in the automated decision rather than how information that was used has been weighted?

The escalation pathway amendment responds to stakeholder feedback that, while the current assessment framework promotes consistent and equitable decision-making through the application of legislated rules, there may be limited circumstances where an assessment outcome does not fully reflect an individual's ageing-related needs. The escalation pathway provides a targeted safeguard for exceptional cases while preserving the benefits of a rules-based assessment system.
